name: Can I live in my house while a home addition is being built?

mainEntity.name: Can I live in my house while a home addition is being built?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether you can stay in your home depends on the scope, location, and structural impact of the addition. For isolated main-floor projects like a family room or bedroom addition, homeowners often remain on-site because temporary dust barriers seal off the construction zone. If your project involves a kitchen expansion, primary bathroom addition, or a second-story build where the roof is temporarily removed, daily utilities and living areas will be disrupted, making temporary off-site lodging much more practical.
acceptedAnswer.description: You can often stay during isolated ground-level additions, but whole-house renovations, major kitchen tie-ins, or second-story projects may require temporary relocation.
